decisions.question: A recorded invocation with files/ and a {package}:{executable} command: `dart run {package}:{executable}` from files/ exits 255 ('Could not find a file named "pubspec.yaml"') whenever pub's mtime check reads the resolution as stale, and neither `dart pub get` nor `dart pub get --enforce-lockfile` refreshes those mtimes when the resolution is unchanged, so ADR-001 item 9's one pub get cannot cure it; this repository reads stale now. How does the cli set run a {package}:{executable} command?

options.label: script under the running dart
options.consequence: Runs `{dart} --packages={root}/.dart_tool/package_config.json {package root}/bin/{executable}.dart {args}` from the case's working directory, the root read from the package configuration: starts on a stale workspace, prints exactly what dart run prints in the same time; ADR-001 item 7 names the command, not how it runs. The governance's stated reason for the pub get is wrong and is reported as a contract gap.

options.label: dart run as the prototype did
options.consequence: Literal to the prototypes, but the twelve committed {package}:{executable} cases with files/ exit 255 at nidana.tooling's gates whenever the workspace reads stale (after any checkout that touches a pubspec but not the lockfile), which reads as the cases' own exit code.

options.label: refresh the mtimes
options.consequence: Touch pubspec.lock and then package_config.json after the pub get so dart run sees a fresh resolution: the tool writes into the workspace's files beyond what ADR-001 states, and depends on pub's private freshness rule.

options.label: stop for the owner
options.consequence: The plan waits on an ADR-001 amendment although an implementation within the ADR's text exists.

decisions.why: The experiment shows dart run from files/ fails on a stale workspace and that no pub command refreshes the mtimes; the script form passes every seeded case fresh and stale and matches dart run's output and time. It stays within ADR-001's text (item 7 names the command; how it runs is the tool's). The governance premise (pub get prevents stale runs) is reported as a contract gap so hsdd-adr can state the form. A careful engineer would have shown the owner this before departing from the prototype.

decisions.question: The file replay's generator command: run as written (the leading `fvm dart` or `dart` replaced) or in the script form of the cli set?

options.label: as written
options.consequence: `{dart} run nidana_dart_codegen:generate ...` from the root, as the scope states; dart run from the root re-resolves a stale workspace silently and runs.

options.label: script form
options.consequence: Uniform with the cli set, but departs from the scope's 'a leading fvm dart or dart running as the dart that runs the tool' with no failure to cure.

decisions.why: The governance states it; from the root dart run works stale or fresh.

decisions.question: 'The backticked span of the contract's - file: bullet that holds {output}' names three spans of topic-codegen@v1's bullet (the command and `{output}` alone twice). Which span is the generator command?

options.label: holds {output} and a space
options.consequence: Exactly one span of the - file: bullets that holds {output} and a space; zero or several fail the replay with a command problem. Picks the command in the committed text and rejects bare placeholders and paths like {output}/x.

options.label: the first span holding {output}
options.consequence: Works on the committed text but picks `{output}` if prose ever names it before the command.

options.label: a span starting with fvm dart or dart
options.consequence: Most permissive to prose; a malformed command is then 'no command' instead of a loud wrong-command failure.

decisions.why: A command has a program and an argument; the rule is crisp and the committed text satisfies it (pinned by a test reading the committed contract).

decisions.question: What counts as a package a recorded invocation's command runs, for PENDING? nidana-checks@v1's eight analyze-* cases run `dart analyze` with the plugin enabled in files/analysis_options.yaml.

options.label: command package, dart run target, enabled plugins
options.consequence: PackageCommand's package, a dart run target's package, and the keys of files/analysis_options.yaml's top-level plugins: section; the analyze-* cases are PENDING until nidana_dart_lint exists, as the phase Verification requires.

options.label: command package only
options.consequence: The analyze-* cases run and fail on dart analyze's exit for a plugin that does not resolve (4), against the phase Verification.

decisions.chosen: command package, dart run target, enabled plugins
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 7 has a case that needs the plugin enable it there, and dart analyze runs the plugin, so the plugin is a package the command runs. Keys are read by hand: package:yaml is not in the tool's ADR-002 row.

decisions.question: For file replays and recorded invocations, which comes first: the restriction or PENDING? (The behavior set has PENDING first.)

options.label: restriction first
options.consequence: A not-admitted replay passes unrun whatever its packages; nidana.tooling.lint.1 to .4 and nidana.tooling.codegen.9 gate on their own shares of nidana-checks@v1 without waiting on the other producer's package; unrestricted replays still report PENDING.

options.label: PENDING first, as behavior
options.consequence: Consistent with nidana.model.6, but each nidana-checks@v1 producer's restricted gate fails on the other producer's cases until that package exists, against ADR-001 Consequences ('no producer waits on another').

options.label: defects after PENDING too
options.consequence: A defective case outside the share would pass silently at the other producer's gates.

decisions.why: ADR-001 item 10 lets a file or cli contract have several producers, each restricting to its share, and item 9 has a not-admitted replay 'not run and counts as passing'. Defects stay first so a contract gap is loud at every gate. Pinned on the committed tree by `nidana-checks --guarantee G1..G8` (8 PENDING, 9 not run).

decisions.question: Admission of a replay that declares no guarantee id (a - file: bullet without a covers clause, a case without a table row).

options.label: runs only unrestricted
options.consequence: Under any restriction it is not run: 'a slug with no id of its own in the restriction runs none of them'.

options.label: vacuously admitted
options.consequence: 'Every id it covers is in the restriction' is vacuously true, so it would run under any restriction, against the item's 'so' clause.

decisions.why: Matches ADR-001 item 9's consequence clause; no committed replay declares none.

decisions.question: How does pub get's failure surface?

options.label: every file and cli set unavailable
options.consequence: Each file and cli set of the replay is SetUnavailable with the reason (exit 2); structure, surface, reject, behavior and schema still run and print, as they do when the analysis fails.

options.label: the whole replay stops
options.consequence: One error line and exit 2 with no fixture lines, hiding the sets that could run.

decisions.chosen: every file and cli set unavailable
decisions.why: Consistent with how an unavailable analysis or runner is reported; the exit code is the same.

decisions.question: Does a generator's non-zero exit fail the file replay when its tree matches?

options.label: fails, beside the tree comparison
options.consequence: An exit problem first, then any tree problems.

options.label: tree only
options.consequence: Literal to ADR-001 item 6's 'runs it ... and compares', but passes a run that failed.

decisions.why: topic-codegen@v1 G3 has generate write the tree; a tree written by a failed run is not that. No committed fixture changes verdict.

decisions.question: Is the tree at a recorded invocation's {output} formatted before it is compared with expected/?

options.label: formatted
options.consequence: 'as item 6 compares', and the prototype formats; generate-no-graph's expected/topics.g.dart is the formatted file replay output.

options.label: not formatted
options.consequence: A raw byte comparison; a generator's unformatted output would fail the case though the file replay passes.

decisions.why: ADR-001 item 7 refers to item 6's comparison, which formats.

decisions.question: The order of replacing a path's given and symlink-resolved forms in a recorded stream.

options.label: longer form first
options.consequence: On macOS /var/... is inside /private/var/...; replacing the longer first never leaves /private{output}.

options.label: given first
options.consequence: Leaves /private{output} and /private{files} for every resolved path.

decisions.why: Shown by S2; ADR-001 item 7 fixes the order across placeholders, not within a pair.

decisions.question: How recorded streams and args are decoded.

options.label: strict for recordings, lenient for process output
options.consequence: A recording that is not UTF-8 is a case defect (no run); process output never crashes the replay.

options.label: lenient for both
options.consequence: Two different invalid byte sequences could compare equal as U+FFFD.

decisions.chosen: strict for recordings, lenient for process output
decisions.why: A recording is a fixture; a process's output is whatever the producer prints.

decisions.question: The args and exit_code forms the cli set accepts.

options.label: split at newlines, one final newline dropped; exit 0 to 255, optional newline
options.consequence: Every committed case fits; an empty line is an empty argument; anything else fails before running.

options.label: trim and skip empty lines as the prototype did
options.consequence: Cannot express an empty argument; hides malformed files.

decisions.chosen: split at newlines, one final newline dropped; exit 0 to 255, optional newline
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 7: one argument per line; all 39 committed cases checked against the rule while planning.

decisions.question: Trees for the byte-for-byte comparisons: from the snapshot or read at run time, and with hidden entries?

options.label: read at run time, hidden entries included
options.consequence: readTree reads expected/ and {output} fully; a .keep in expected/ counts (the routed S101 item); links read through; directories not compared.

options.label: from the snapshot
options.consequence: The snapshot drops hidden entries, which the routed item forbids, and would load every expected/ tree into memory for every set.

decisions.chosen: read at run time, hidden entries included
decisions.why: Routed from S101; dart format skips hidden files (F1), so they compare as written.

decisions.question: A process timeout for generator and command runs (routed weigh item).

options.label: no timeout, left routed
options.consequence: As every runner today; Process.run gives a child an end of input on stdin, so waiting for input cannot hang.

options.label: a fixed timeout
options.consequence: Needs a value and an outcome class (FAIL or ERROR) the governance does not give, and Process.start plumbing and tests.

decisions.why: ADR-001 requires none; I1 removes the commonest hang; routed to the first gate with timers or isolates.

decisions.question: Where the new process code lives, and lenientUtf8 (routed).

options.label: processes.dart and command_runs.dart
options.consequence: processes.dart is the one way any process starts (lenientUtf8 moved there); command_runs.dart runs the two sets; runners.dart stays the behavior runner; purity_test pins five dart:io libraries.

options.label: everything in runners.dart
options.consequence: One process library, but the behavior runner and the command runs mix, and runners.dart grows past what one review reads.

options.label: everything in shell.dart
options.consequence: shell.dart is already 603 lines; nidana.model.6 split the runner out for this phase.

decisions.why: Each file one responsibility; the routed lenientUtf8 item asks for one place every process uses.
evidence: hsdd/verify/nidana.model.6.verification.md Observed (the runner moved out of shell.dart)

decisions.question: How to narrow the read of a suite slug (routed _snapshotsOf item).

options.label: partial snapshots of the suite files
options.consequence: The shell reads only the suite files into a snapshot that holds them alone; the planner is unchanged; an absent or dangling suite file fails its binding.

options.label: a path-keyed suites map
options.consequence: A cleaner planner signature, but every behavior_test plan call (9 sites) changes.

options.label: leave routed
options.consequence: A read defect in another slug's tree keeps ending the replay with no fixture line.

decisions.why: Fixes the defect with the least churn; this phase's verification doc corrects nidana.model.6's statement.

decisions.question: A contract text that is not UTF-8 (routed): take it in this phase?

options.label: take it, Task 1
options.consequence: decodeSource as for Dart sources; a structure contract-text failure (exit 1); the restriction check reads ids from a lenient decoding.

options.label: leave routed
options.consequence: Exit 2 for a fixture defect stays; no later tool phase exists to take it.

decisions.question: The test harness for the two sets.

options.label: stand-in generator package gen in a seeded workspace
options.consequence: A dependency-free member whose generate writes unformatted Dart, prints paths, exits 2 on usage, and with --write-then-fail writes and exits 1; resolved offline, its pub get needs no network; the samples were validated case by case.

contract_gaps.where: item 9, 'Before the file or cli set, the tool runs dart pub get --enforce-lockfile once ... so that no case runs on a stale resolution'; item 7, the {package}:{executable} command; and hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md nidana.model.7 Scope (4), which gives as its reason that dart run from a files/ directory re-resolves a stale workspace and fails with exit 255
contract_gaps.problem: On Dart 3.13.5 dart pub get --enforce-lockfile (and dart pub get) rewrites neither pubspec.lock nor .dart_tool/package_config.json when the resolution is unchanged, so it does not make a stale workspace fresh: dart run {package}:{executable} from a files/ directory still exits 255 ('Could not find a file named "pubspec.yaml"'), which reads as the case's exit code. Freshness is pub's mtime rule (every pubspec.yaml no newer than pubspec.lock, pubspec.lock no newer than package_config.json), and this repository reads stale now. Twelve committed cases are affected: topic-codegen@v1's catalog-not-a-package, generate-graph-not-json, generate-graph-undecodable and generate-usage-output-is-a-file, and nidana-checks@v1's eight scan-* cases with files/. Evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/file-cli-sets-plan/ staleness-output.txt K1 to K8, staleness2-output.txt M1 to M5, staleness3-output.txt N1 to N8.
contract_gaps.proposed_fix: hsdd-adr amends ADR-001 item 7: a {package}:{executable} command runs as the running dart with --packages={workspace root}/.dart_tool/package_config.json on bin/{executable}.dart of the package's root as that configuration gives it, from the case's working directory (which runs on a stale workspace and prints what dart run prints). Item 9's pub get bullet keeps its rule with its reason restated: it keeps the lockfile and the package configuration consistent with the pubspecs, so a case never runs on a resolution the lockfile does not hold. nidana.model.7's Scope (4) gets the same restatement through hsdd-spec. The plan already implements the form (its decision 1), so the amendment changes no code.

contract_gaps.where: ## Validation, the scan cases' paragraph: 'files/ itself holds no pubspec.yaml, so that dart run from it finds the workspace's package configuration and resolves nothing in place'
contract_gaps.problem: That holds only on a workspace whose mtimes read fresh; on a stale one dart run from files/ fails with exit 255 before the scan starts (same evidence as the ADR-001 gap). No fixture changes: the replay tool runs the cases in the script form, which reads the workspace's package configuration from files/ either way.
contract_gaps.proposed_fix: A compatible hsdd-contract touch within v1 restating the sentence as: files/ holds no pubspec.yaml, so the scan, run from it, reads the workspace's package configuration and resolves nothing in place; the replay tool runs the command as ADR-001 item 7 states. Can ride the ADR-001 amendment.
